description: Confidentiality survival: 3 years vs 4 years. One-year difference on a HIGH topic — defensible to flag or not.

company_clauses.text: The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Section 9 shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years.

vendor_clauses.text: The confidentiality obligations under this Section 10 shall survive any termination of this Agreement and continue in full force and effect for a period of four (4) years following such termination.

expected_conflicts.notes: Longer confidentiality protection favors the disclosing party. In bilateral agreements both parties disclose, so the longer period (vendor's 4 years) is slightly more protective for both sides. Defensible to flag as LOW (minor inconsistency) or to skip (substantively equivalent). HIGH is the rubric-tier for confidentiality so also defensible.

rubric_notes: Same structure (post-termination survival), different duration. Without trade-secret carve-outs to compare, the 1-year gap is small. The agent that recommends retaining vendor's 4-year language as marginally more protective is showing senior judgment; the agent that no-flags it as immaterial is also defensible.
